rationale:
A page marked pages.rebuild_policy='owned' — a tool/widget-owned page, or a runtime-fill shell — is selected by a GENERIC page-composition loop, fully recomposed by an LLM, git-committed over the live page, and only THEN refused by the ownership guard in save_page_sections. The guard works. It protects the DATABASE ROW, and the commit that replaces the file the site actually serves has already run. Net: the live tool is destroyed while page_components still describes it, and no rerender repairs that because content_data still describes the old page.

This is bugs_open/208, filed 2026-08-06 by another lane during pre-flight for an owner-authorised full rebuild of ai-agent-orchestration.com. The dispatch was NOT fired because of it.

Why guard rail 1 did not already cover this, precisely. Migration 164 created rebuild_policy and named exactly two Go refusals — ReconcileSitePlanAction emits owned_page_review instead of needs_page, and save_page_sections hard-refuses. Those are sufficient for the route 164 modelled: needs_page -> page-build-handler, whose live order is save_sections -> update_status -> deploy_page, so the refusal precedes any commit. Verified 2026-08-06: all 158 needs_page rows fleet-wide, all history, route to page-build-handler. 164 simply did not model a path that selects straight off pages.build_status. Three agents do exactly that and invert the order: page-rebuild, pageflow-builder and site-work-orchestrator all run assemble_page -> deploy_page (git_commit) -> save_sections.

Exposure, measured on the live DB 2026-08-06: 14 active owned pages at needs_rebuild/planned across 6 domains. 13 of them currently serve working tools (HTTP 200, 5-7 script blocks, 2-15 interactive elements) — including tool-arena-interface and tool-gauntlet on vonc.com, which is the site of the 'vonc arena clobber' that motivated the ownership marker in the first place. The marker still is not protecting the page whose destruction created it. A further ~189 owned pages sit at 'deployed': not selected today, but selected by the include_all branch, which drops the status filter entirely.

The damage is not yet realised and that is measured, not assumed: all 13 served bodies were fetched and hashed pre-fix (BASELINE_2026-08-06_owned_pages_served.txt) and none has the shape of generic regenerated prose. So this is a fix before the fire, and the baseline is the control set for verifying it.

A second, unreported symptom decided the SHAPE of the fix. continue_on_error is unset on all four build loops, and shouldContinueLoopOnError (loop_error_handler.go:70-90) requires it, so an error inside an iteration fails the WHOLE workflow. Pages are selected ORDER BY nav_order, name. So today the existing refusal does not merely lose the owned page — it strands every page positioned after it. Any refusal added here must therefore be a SKIP, not an error.

The intent is to make the destructive state unreachable rather than caught late, at the two ends of the generic path: an owned page never ENTERS a generic build selection (default-off opt-in to override), and if it enters anyway it cannot be COMPOSED, using the skip protocol that already exists so that git_commit and every agent config stay untouched.

plan.summary: bugs_open/208: a rebuild_policy='owned' page swept into a generic composition loop is git-committed over the live tool one step BEFORE the ownership guard refuses the DB write. Refuse it at both ends of the generic path instead: exclude owned pages at SELECTION (both branches of queryPagesForBuild, behind a default-off include_owned opt-in), and refuse COMPOSITION at assemble_page using the action's existing skipped:true protocol - which git_commit already honours, so no agent config changes - then thread that skip through save_page_sections and update_page_status so one owned page no longer strands the whole batch or falsely stamps itself deployed.

edits.rationale: Layer 1, selection: an owned page should never enter a generic composition loop at all. The predicate goes in BOTH branches — the status-filtered one and include_all, which has no status filter and would otherwise sweep the ~189 owned pages at 'deployed'. Gated by a new step-config key include_owned whose UNSAFE value is the non-default, per owner ruling 2026-08-02 s2 (a seam licensed by 'callers must all be X' gets a field with the unsafe default OFF, because a comment is not a control on a tree this many sessions share). Nothing live sets it: both live consumers carry only include_all and build_statuses. COALESCE is deliberate even though the column is NOT NULL today — a bare <> would drop NULL-policy rows if that default is ever relaxed, which is the same silent-omission shape being fixed. Also reports what was withheld (census + owned_pages_excluded on the result) so an exclusion is never silent.

The shared half, so the three touch points cannot drift apart: page identity resolution across the two loop-variable shapes (current_page.* for the two page loops, current_item.spec.* for the work-item loop), the policy read, the review-item emitter, and the upstream-skip reader. Kept in a helper rather than inlined per caller because a precondition parked in a caller is one port away from gone (the lesson recorded on bugs_closed/145). The emitter reuses reconcile's EXISTING owned_page_review item_type and item_key namespace ('owned_page_review:'+name, ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING) rather than inventing an item type, so repeated dispatches converge on one row and dedup against reconcile's items for free. Emission errors are logged and swallowed: a guard must never fail because its reporting failed.

Layer 2, and the arm that makes the git commit unreachable for every current AND future compose-then-commit pipeline, including work items already sitting in the table that Layer 1 cannot retract. assemble_page is the correct seam, measured rather than assumed: it has EXACTLY three live consumers and they are exactly the three agents whose order is assemble_page -> deploy_page -> save_sections, and all three feed it freshly LLM-written HTML (content_field page_content.response.page_html). Critically it is NOT the wider net: gating git_commit instead would break the only paths owned pages legitimately deploy by — page-rerender (rerender_single_page) and section-editor (apply_section_edit) both git_commit pages, and migration 164 says re-assembly of existing page_components 'is deliberately NOT gated - it is how owned pages deploy'. The refusal uses the action's OWN existing skip shape, which git_commit already honours via checkUpstreamSkipped, so no agent config changes anywhere; and it must be a skip rather than an error because no build loop sets continue_on_error.

Without this the skip dies one step later and the batch dies with it: the action has no upstream-skip check, resolves the page name from current_page.name (which survives an assembly skip), reaches its own ownership refusal and returns a HARD ERROR — which with continue_on_error unset fails the whole workflow and strands every remaining page. So the pre-fix cost of one owned page in the set was the operator's entire rebuild. This does NOT weaken the existing refusal: it fires only when the assembly itself was skipped, so an owned page arriving WITH content (an older image, or a future path that bypasses assemble_page) still meets the loud refusal unchanged.

After an ownership skip nothing was assembled and nothing was committed, so stamping build_status='deployed' claims work that did not happen — and it is worse than cosmetic: the same statement writes built_from_plan_version = the current plan, which makes ReconcileSitePlanAction's decideEmit return skip_built and PERMANENTLY suppresses the owned_page_review item that is this design's own visibility channel. The existing deploy guards cannot catch this: an owned page HAS components (its tool) and typically no planned sections, so both pageHasComponents and pageSectionShortfall pass. Deliberately keyed to THIS guard's skip marker and not to any assembly skip: a generic page whose content generation failed is also stamped deployed today, which is its own defect, but un-stamping it would change retry behaviour on the fleet's main build path (the page would be re-selected every run) — a wider blast radius than this bug, so it is filed separately rather than smuggled in, and pinned by a test that fails if someone widens the condition.

WriteBuildItemsAction is the second Go caller of the same shared helper and a producer of needs_page items, so it inherits the exclusion by passing includeOwned=false — the same refusal reconcile already makes for its own route. Stated honestly in the comment: whether such an item is DANGEROUS depends on its consumer, and the two differ (page-build-handler saves before it deploys and is safe; site-work-orchestrator's loop commits first). Not filing the item makes the difference irrelevant. No config surface added here, matching reconcile.

edits.rationale: sqlmock tests written so that REMOVING each guard makes a NAMED test fail — proven by four mutations, not asserted. Where a guard's job is to NOT act (not commit, not stamp), the negative is enforced by giving sqlmock no expectation for the forbidden query. Includes the negative controls that a guard-everything implementation would fail: a generic page must still assemble, and an ordinary content-failure skip must NOT be claimed by the ownership branch. One test was strengthened after mutation M3 showed it passing with the guard deleted — SavePageSectionsAction's pre-existing 'page not found' branch returns the identical {skipped:true} shape, so the assertion had to move to the discriminating reason field; logged in WRONG_CALLS.md.

grounded_in: get_pages_to_build_actions.go queryPagesForBuild, pre-fix: `WHERE site_id = $1 AND status = 'active' AND COALESCE(build_status, 'planned') IN (...)` — `grep -n rebuild_policy get_pages_to_build_actions.go` returns nothing, and the include_all branch has no status filter at all. This is the selection defect.

Migration 164 (docs/agent_docs/sql_for_agents/164_pages_rebuild_policy.sql) header: 'the generic rebuild paths (reconcile -> needs_page -> page-build-handler -> save_page_sections DELETE+reinsert) clobber it - the vonc arena clobber is the proof', and it names exactly two Go refusals. This is why the route it modelled is safe and a build_status-driven path was never covered.

Migration 164, same header: 'page_rerender / assemble (re-assembly of EXISTING page_components) is deliberately NOT gated - it is how owned pages deploy.' This is what rules out putting the guard in git_commit, which page-rerender and section-editor both use.

Live agent_definitions, nested walk 2026-08-06: action assemble_page has exactly three consumers - page-rebuild, pageflow-builder, site-work-orchestrator - and in all three next_step is deploy_page and output_field is 'assembled_page'. The same three are the only agents whose order is assemble_page -> deploy_page (git_commit) -> save_sections.

Live agent_definitions 2026-08-06: page-build-handler's order is plan_sections -> validate_content -> save_sections -> update_status -> spawn_rerender_agent -> deploy_page, i.e. it SAVES BEFORE IT DEPLOYS; and page-rerender's is rerender_sections -> save_sections -> render_page -> deploy_page. So commit-before-save is not the platform convention - it is confined to the three loops above.

git_deployer_actions.go checkUpstreamSkipped:576-588 reads collectedData['assembled_page'].skipped as its FIRST branch, and multipage_actions.go:38-62 already returns {html:'', skipped:true, skip_reason:...} in two existing cases. So a refusal expressed as a skip needs no change to git_commit and no config change on any agent.

loop_error_handler.go:66-80 shouldContinueLoopOnError requires the loop step's continue_on_error; live config shows it UNSET on all four build loops (page-rebuild.build_pages_loop, pageflow-builder.build_pages_loop, site-work-orchestrator.build_items_loop and .fix_items_loop). With ORDER BY nav_order, name, the existing hard refusal therefore strands every page after the owned one.

Live census 2026-08-06: 14 active pages are rebuild_policy='owned' AND build_status IN ('needs_rebuild','planned') across 6 domains, including tool-arena-interface and tool-gauntlet on vonc.com; ~189 further owned pages sit at 'deployed' and would be selected by the include_all branch.

Served-state baseline 2026-08-06 (BASELINE_2026-08-06_owned_pages_served.txt): 13 of the 14 return HTTP 200 with 5-7 <script> blocks and 2-15 interactive elements - the tools are intact, so the damage is not yet realised. The 14th, vonc.com/blog/provocation.html, is a 404 with 0 page_components - and it is the ONLY page the exclusion removes from a live selection set, so the no-op case is measured too.

Live proof of the predicate by row identity, ai-agent-orchestration.com needs_rebuild set: old predicate returns 5 rows, new predicate 3. agent-complexity-estimator and password-entropy (both owned, page_type=tool) drop out; three generic blog-post pages remain - the negative control against a predicate that excludes everything.

reconcile_site_plan_action.go:232-270 is the framework's existing response to an owned page reaching a generic builder: exclude it and INSERT a site_work_items row of item_type='owned_page_review', status='needs_human_review', item_key='owned_page_review:'+name, ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING. This change reuses that namespace rather than inventing an item type.

site_work_items 2026-08-06: all 158 needs_page rows fleet-wide (all history) have handler_agent='page-build-handler', the safe consumer. site-work-orchestrator's load_work_items filters handler_agent='page-content-writer', and the 14 items it has consumed are literal_markdown/placeholder_contact - of which 11 target rebuild_policy='owned' pages on webdesign.co.uk, all failed. So the third loop really does receive owned pages; the route is discovery-check fix items, not needs_page.

UpdatePageStatusAction (v3_site_actions.go): the deployed branch writes built_from_plan_version = the site's current plan. reconcile_site_plan_action.go:210-214 decideEmit returns skip_built on that stamp, which suppresses the owned_page_review emission - so a false deployed stamp after a skip would silence the design's own visibility channel. The existing deploy guards cannot catch it because an owned page has components and no planned sections.
plan.risks:
Behaviour change to name, not hide: an owned page that an operator explicitly names in a bulk rebuild is now REFUSED rather than rebuilt, and it stays at needs_rebuild with an open owned_page_review item instead of being silently stamped deployed. That is the intended semantics (an owned page's route is the tool pipeline or apply_section_edit), but it is a guarantee change for features_open/021's operator bulk rebuild, which went LIVE 2026-08-06 and is owned by a different workstream - named here and being told, per owner ruling 2026-07-29 s3, rather than merely measured.

Fail-open posture, chosen deliberately and inherited from the guard it extends: an unresolvable page, a nil DB or a scan error means the guard STANDS DOWN and the page assembles as before. A fail-closed guard here would stop generic page building fleet-wide the first time the query hiccupped, which is worse than the harm it prevents, and Layer 1 already carries the load for the two loops with most of the traffic. save_page_sections' existing guard states the same rule ('a scan error means an older schema, in which case the guard stands down').

Emission volume: one deterministic item_key per page (owned_page_review:<name>) with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING against the (site_id, item_key) partial unique index over open statuses, bounded by owned pages per site (14 fleet-wide today). This is NOT the shape of bugs_open/204's 114-junk-items-per-site incident, which had no stable key and an unbounded population. The honest fallback if the review-queue owner objects is log-plus-result-field only, since reconcile already files the same item on its next pass.

The censusExcludedOwnedPages query adds one extra SELECT per get_pages_to_build call, and one INSERT per excluded page. On a site with no owned pages it is a single indexed count-zero query.

Not attempted, and stated so it is not mistaken for an oversight: reordering save_sections before deploy_page (it would change commit/save ordering for every page on three pipelines, and deploy_page's page_deployed.commit_sha is consumed downstream by update_page_status); adding continue_on_error to the loops (a config change to tolerate failures by default, which is the wrong default); and un-stamping ordinary content-failure skips (correct, but a fleet-wide retry-behaviour change beyond this bug - filed separately).

Inert until the chassis image rolls: Go only, no DB config half, so there is no ordering hazard between halves and no seed to apply.
